Getting Started

WHY INNOVATE?
But then they ask, ‘Which of these opportunities fits me, fits this company, puts to work what we (or I) are good at and have shown capacity for in performance?

FINDING PROBLEMS WORTH SOLVING
Components of Innovation
The components of innovation include:
A problem worth solving
A solution that solves the problem
A business case that allows the solution to enter the market and to scale
All must be validated
Is the problem worth working on?
Does the solution address the problem effectively and efficiently?
Does the business case allow the solution to move forward and does it work for all stakeholders?
Finding Good Problems
Innovation and entrepreneurship begin with finding problems worth solving
Because not all problems are of equal value or importance
What are good problems?
Per Frans Johansson, the best innovative ideas are those which are new and valuable
Those that create a new future
How do you find them?

And we get out of our heads by searching at different boundaries of uncertainty for opportunities: 
from the present forward (“What’s probable? What’s plausible?”) and 
from the future back (“What’s possible?
